study.title: Automated catheter segmentation and tip detection in cerebral angiography with topology-aware geometric deep learning

imaging.modality_detail: X-ray fluoroscopy sequences with DSA roadmapping mask frames (contrast and non-contrast) used as additional input
imaging.territory_detail: cerebral angiography (catheter/guidewire up to intracranial internal carotid artery)

public_dataset_used.detail: novel in-house annotated fluoroscopy dataset due to lack of public data

data_released.detail: Data available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: MD/PhD student (6 years of experience) supervised by an experienced imaging scientist (15 years)

task.task_description: Frame-by-frame segmentation of the complete catheter/guidewire structure in cerebral angiography fluoroscopy and tip position tracking derived from skeletonized masks; comparison of input schemes with DSA roadmap masks.
task.clinical_application: AI augmentation and automation of robotic neurointervention (catheter visualization and tip tracking)

architecture_names: TAG-DL (rotation-reflection equivariant UNet, D4 group convolutions, centerline-Dice loss)

temporal_evidence.quote: current frame with a non- contrast mask frame as second channel; (3) current frame with a non- contrast mask frame subtracted prior to input as one channel

G1.quote: Due to the lack of publicly available data, we developed a novel annotated fluoroscopy dataset to support this study.

G2.quote: our dataset is limited to a single center and fluoroscopy vendor, and exclusively reflects diagnostic cerebral angiography

G5.quote: Manual annotation of the complete catheter structure is considerably more laborious than annotating the tip alone, which has been a significant barrier to generating suitable datasets.

G9.quote: sparsity of catheter pixels (<2%) compared with background pixels

other_limitations: Restricted to fully radio-opaque diagnostic devices (0.035 inch guidewire, 5 Fr catheters)
False-positive detections of contrast and other wire-like structures
Failure to detect large sections of catheter body
Centerline Dice treats all centerline regions as equally important
future_work: Incorporate tip-distance error into the loss function
Generalize to additional devices, especially partially radiolucent therapeutic devices
Add more data with extraneous implants and lines; spline-fitting post-processing
Pre-training on external data and fine-tuning to new scenarios
Development in animal models (pigs) for robotic neurointervention
Evaluation across fluoroscopy systems including robotic systems with haptic feedback
